title: Writing reports and memos

body.text: Have Claude draft a report from
raw data + the structure you want + the audience
— say who's reading (executives like it short, the team likes detail) and the result fits the audience right away.

example: "Write a memo to executives from these sales figures: no more than one page, start with the conclusion, then three reasons, then a recommendation"

title: Structure first, content later

body.text: have the AI propose an outline first, approve it, then write the full text
— fixing an outline is easier than fixing 10 pages of content, and it keeps the report on point.

example: "First, propose an outline for the quarterly results report — don't write the content yet, let me adjust the structure first"

question: What information helps the AI write a report that hits the mark?

options.text: The raw data, the structure you want, and the audience

question: What should a memo to executives be like?

options.text: Short, starting with the conclusion, then the reasons

question: Why ask for an outline before writing the full text?

options.text: Fixing the structure is easier than fixing long content
It makes the AI work slower

question: To write a good report, where should you start?

options.text: Write it all at once with no structure
Write from the end to the front
Lay out the structure first, then fill in the content

question: Why lay out the structure before writing?

options.text: It makes the content organized and easy to read
